title: Flash Answers hypothesis canvas
content:
Working canvas for a lightweight product experiment: 'Flash Answers' — extremely short, prioritized answers (<=40 tokens) surfaced where users need a quick, confident result with an option to expand to the full answer. Rough scratchpad; lots of open questions.

Overview:
- Problem: many product flows surface long generative responses that take >300ms on average and cost more tokens than necessary for quick tasks. Users in quick workflows (search, inline help, inbox triage) often only need a concise assertion or pointer.
- Opportunity: provide an explicitly tiny response mode that optimizes for latency, deterministic brevity, and cost. Offer an expand/fallback to detailed answer or citations.

Hypothesis:
- If we surface a one-line/one-paragraph 'Flash Answer' with a 40-token budget and strong confidence signals, then users will complete quick tasks faster, have fewer back-and-forths, and host token costs per query will drop by ~30% for targeted flows.

Design principles (quick):
- Predictability: always cap tokens strictly, avoid trailing ellipses.
- Explicit affordance: UI shows ‘Flash’ and an expand chevron to full answer.
- Conservative content: prefer high-precision short facts, avoid hallucinated claims.
- Fast path: route to lowest-latency compatible model/variant first; fallback to full model if user expands or confidence low.

Product variants to explore:
1) Flash-only: user asks, gets Flash answer; expand for details.
2) Dual stream: start streaming Flash token(s) immediately, then stream rest if expand selected (visual continuity).
3) Suggested flash: system suggests flash answers in lists (search results, inbox preview).

Technical notes / rough infra plan:
- New response mode flag: response_mode: "flash" with token_budget=40 and response_style=concise.
- Confidence heuristics: model logit-based entropy + prompt-level calibration layer to tag low-confidence flashes.
- Routing: route to quantized small model variant (e.g., 7B q4) with fast kernels, unless user has enterprise policy requiring larger models.
- Caching: prefix-level cache for repeated short prompts.

UX sketch (notes-to-self):
- Minimal card: bold one-line answer, tiny source pill(s) if applicable, chevron to expand.
- Fade-in animation when expanding to avoid jarring transition.
- Preserve conversation history: Flash stays as a separate turn with an "expanded" child turn when user opens it.

Acceptance considerations (safety/quality):
- No novel factual claims without citation for constrained domains (medical, legal).
- If model confidence below threshold, show "Short answer uncertain — expand for details" rather than a potentially wrong flash.

Risks:
- Users may over-trust short answers. Need explicit cues about uncertainty and easy path to long-form evidence.
- Short form may increase clicks/expands, potentially not reducing total token spend. Need to measure net cost changes.

Experiment ideas:
- A/B test in product search preview: Flash vs baseline snippet for queries with explicit intent for quick answers (e.g., factual queries, code snippet requests).
- Metric buckets: users who click expand; time-to-first-click; task completion within 30s; token spend per successful interaction.

Open notes / TODOs:
- Define reliable confidence signal (ask applied-ml for heuristics).
- Prototype response_mode flag in the SDK + console toggle.
- Design mockups for mobile and desktop with product design.
- List of sensitive domains where Flash should be disabled by default.

Quick personal checklist:
- [ ] Spike routing to 7B quantized instance for 40-token cap. (eng: Mika)
- [ ] Draft UX mock for search/storybook. (design: Sam)
- [ ] Write experiment spec & tracking plan. (me)

Notes to self: avoid over-optimizing for cost at expense of perceived correctness. The product goal is better speed+clarity for quick tasks, not purely token-minimization. Keep it progressively enhancing: Flash should be conservative by default.

Small sign-off language for experiment card: "Short, confident answer — expand for more. Powered by Flash Answers (experimental)."
user_stories: As a power user, I want a one-line answer so I can triage emails quickly without reading a long reply.
As a mobile user, I want search previews to show instant short answers so I can decide which result to open.
As a developer integrating the API, I want a response_mode flag to request 'flash' outputs with strict token budget.
As a product manager, I want to measure whether flash answers reduce time-to-task and token spend for targeted flows.
acceptance_criteria: Flash answers are capped at 40 tokens and never stream beyond the cap in flash mode.
UI shows an explicit expand affordance and an uncertainty indicator when confidence is below threshold.
Server-side routing honors enterprise policy for model size and does not route to smaller models for restricted customers.
Experiment instrumentation records expand rate, task completion, and token spend per session.
Quality guardrails prevent flash mode in medically or legally sensitive queries by default.
metrics: Expand rate (percent of flash answers where user expands)
Median time-to-accept (time from flash shown to user signal of completion)
Token spend per successful micro-task (baseline vs flash cohort)
CPU/GPU p99 latency for flash route
open_questions: What confidence threshold is reliable enough to show a flash without sources? (need ML spike)
Do we allow partial cites (single-source pill) in flash or only when confidence high?
How to handle multimodal flashes (image caption as a flash)?
What policies should disable flash by default (PHI, PII, legal)?
Will flash reduce net token spend or simply shift tokens to follow-up expands?
next_steps: Book 3-session spike with applied-ml to iterate confidence heuristic (owner: Mika)
Prototype SDK flag and backend route for flash mode (owner: eng spike)
Draft experiment spec and expected effect sizes (owner: Rafael)
Create a short internal one-pager for stakeholder alignment and privacy review
